## Goal
Implement the requested change from the agent mention.

## Original request
> > You’re right. The current #202 policy is too conservative for how this repo actually works.
> > The safety rule should not be “non-draft + default branch only.” It should be closer to:
> > `current-head self-approval + checks/mergeability pass + no requested changes + approved head still matches -> merge into the PR’s configured base`
> > That means two changes to #202’s design:
> > 
> > 1. **Draft agent PRs should be eligible**
> >    
> >    * Agent-created PRs are commonly draft during automation.
> >    * Once `agent-self-approve` has approved the exact current head and checks pass, draft status should not be a terminal blocker.
> >    * The self-merge workflow can deterministically mark the PR ready before merging, but only for trusted agent PRs/branches.
> > 2. **Stacked PRs should be mergeable into their base branch**
> >    
> >    * The current default-branch guard in [`self-merge.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/daee1f9c7fe9e671688b32d0f1d3cbbbf97e71ad/.agent/src/self-merge.ts#L254-L260) would block normal stacked agent PRs.
> >    * For this repo, if [Add opt-in self-merge after self-approval #202](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/202) is based on [Polish self-approval status handling #186](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/186)’s branch, self-merge should be allowed to merge [Add opt-in self-merge after self-approval #202](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/202) into [Polish self-approval status handling #186](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/186)’s branch after the same approval/check/head guards pass.
> >    * We still need to reject unsafe bases, such as fork bases or unknown branches, but not same-repo stacked agent bases.
> > 
> > I’d revise #202 with a small follow-up fix:
> > 
> > * Replace the draft hard block with “draft is allowed for trusted agent PRs; mark ready before merge.”
> > * Replace the default-branch-only guard with “allow default branch or same-repo PR stack base.”
> > * Keep the important guards: `AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_MERGE`, current-head self-approval, no requested changes, green/pending checks handling, mergeability, and `--match-head-commit`.
> > 
> > So yes: your simpler model is the right product behavior. The implementation should support the repo’s actual workflow: agent draft PRs and stacked PRs are first-class, not exceptions.
> 

@sepo-agent /implement 
I'd recommend further simplify the guardrails for now; let's start with simple implementations with the core function implemented first

## Acceptance criteria
- Implement the requested change.
- Preserve existing behavior unless the request requires a change.
- Update tests or validation as needed.

---

Requested via issue_comment at https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/202

Implemented issue #206 by simplifying the self-merge resolver on top of the #202 self-merge stack: draft PRs are marked ready without trusted-agent-branch gating, non-default bases are no longer blocked or looked up, and self-merge now relies on the core current-head self-approval, requested-changes, checks, mergeability, and match-head guards.
